svg.title: macOS · Guided clip (experimental) · moment step in the rail · 1000×700
svg.desc: Mirrors App/GuidedBuilderView.swift (railLayout · stretchStep · framingStage · flowStrip) and App/GuidedFramingBox.swift + App/GuidedCanvasFrame.swift — a recorded moment answered on the steps rail, as reworked after the 2026-08-12 mac UI review. The rail carries the answers already given (step 1 done, checkmark, "9:16 · 100× streaks"; the current row writes back "½× slow motion · pan" the moment a control is touched). THE STAGE ALWAYS SHOWS A PICTURE: while the framing is Wide it draws the MOMENT'S OWN exact frame at the canvas (GuidedCanvasFrame anchored just inside the stretch, badge "Moment 1 — exact · as shot", caption "Wide — the whole canvas renders. Pick a punch to frame this stretch.") — never the old dashed placeholder; a punch swaps the same stage to the GuidedFramingBox drawn here: the momentModeChips row (Start framing / End framing / Preview — a still punch reads Framing / Preview) + Drift thru/Eased chips above it, the reserved dashed "✦ Suggest framing" seat top-right, the exact decoded frame dimmed outside the aspect-locked amber box with 8 handles, badge "2.0× · 1 080 px", the pointer grammar caption, and the role caption ("The pan drifts from the start framing to the end framing across the whole stretch." / a still reads "Arrives with the transition and holds this framing for the whole stretch."). SPEED honesty per the same review: chips are gated with a 2% density tolerance (GuidedPlanner.gatedSpeedChips) so a probed ~99.6 fps burst still counts as the 100 fps class — ¼× stays offered at 25 fps output and the racing chips stay out; everything displayed speaks the FLOORED speed that renders (displaySpeed, snapped onto ¼×/½× within 5%), so a seeded ¼× that 50 fps output can only honour as ½× reads ½× in the rail, lights the ½× chip, and adds the accent explainer drawn here: "¼× wants 200 fps of footage — this burst is 100 fps, so at 50 fps output it tops out at ½×. A lower output rate on the Review step unlocks it." HOW IT ARRIVES keeps the welded-ramp copy, and a clamped ease leads the section in accent semibold (desc-only state). The OVERVIEW STRIP above the bottom bar shows the whole clip with Moment 1's ink block outlined in accent and a viewfinder glyph once punched; blocks for answered steps are clickable. Chips: selected = white on accent, unselected = white card; active speed chip = LL.ink + amber. On macOS the SCROLL WHEEL zooms the punch about the box centre (NSEvent local monitor gated on hover, re-armed every body pass) and the pointer changes over the box — open hand inside, resizeUpDown/resizeLeftRight on edge handles, crosshair on corners. Same-day follow-up: the output rate is now ALSO asked on step one (OUTPUT RATE menu above OPENING; the rail writes it back — "9:16 · 50 fps · 100× streaks"), the rail rows scroll when a multi-burst shoot outgrows the window, back-jumps keep later checkmarks clickable (maxVisitedStep), and the floating pill shows no tab highlighted during the flow. Verified 2026-08-12 on the Mac (1660×1183 + the 760×680 stacked fallback) and the iPad Pro 13-inch sim (25 fps output: ¼× offered and highlighted, no gate note). 2026-08-12 scrub-preview follow-up (App/GuidedScrubPreview.swift): the framing-target row is now momentModeChips — drawn here as Start framing (selected) / End framing / Preview (unselected); Preview answers nothing so it never marks the step touched, and the stage column sits at its code-true leading edge (answers 380pt + 32pt spacing → x 714) so the three chips fit the window. DESC-ONLY STATES, not drawn: (1) Preview mode (previewingMoment) — the curve chips + exact-frame box give way to momentPreviewStage: the output-shaped ≈ scrub pane (GuidedScrubDisplay — the step's slice of the finished clip through the crop that renders, black letterbox, bottom-leading black-55% capsule badge "≈ preview · 16s of 21s" in white bold 10pt) with the 22pt GuidedScrubStrip under it at exactly the pane's width (white card capsule; 9pt semibold secondary window-end times on the finished clip's clock, e.g. "2.1s" … "19s"; centred accent eye glyph + "Preview" 10pt semibold while idle; a 14pt accent knob with a 1.5pt white ring while scrubbed) — behaviour exactly as ipad-scrubbed.png; the pane itself scrubs (GuidedPaneScrub: drag anywhere across the picture, and on the Mac hovering peeks) and the hint reads "Hover or drag across the picture to scrub — framing edits stay on the exact-frame box." (2) The locked ✕ — a finished drag locks the preview and a secondary xmark.circle.fill appears trailing OUTSIDE the bar; tapping it lets the frame go. (3) macOS hover-to-peek on both strip and pane — a hover scrubs but clears on exit unless a drag locked it. (4) iOS's axis-classified pane drag (first movement sideways = scrub, vertical = the survey's scroll) — the iPhone/iPad counterpart, no mac behaviour. ALSO desc-only: the WIDE (unpunched) stage now carries the same GuidedScrubStrip under its exact-frame pane (GuidedScrubOverlay in wideStage; pane scrub allowed there because off the canvas step the frame is read-only context), per ipad-moment.png.

g.text: One ramp — the speed change and the framing move ride it together,
in seconds of the finished clip.

output it tops out at ½×. A lower output rate on the Review step
Drag to position · handles resize · scroll wheel
